clue.text: Instruments in drawing room for conventional fogies

definitions.meaning: triangular rulers used by draughtsmen at a drawing board
a group (set) of old-fashioned, conventional people (squares)

explanation.surface: Something in the drawing room suits staid old-fashioned folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing room' suggests a parlour, but here it is a room where technical drawing is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmen's triangles share a name with a clique of stuffy, unfashionable people.

clue.text: Daily guillotined, it's raised-in the house

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards
a guillotine takes off the head, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: The Times is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper is cut down and propped up somewhere in the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guillotined' removes the T of TIMES, leaving IMES; 'raised' turns that upwards in this down entry to give SEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is short for a semi-detached dwelling, one of a pair joined by a shared wall.

clue.text: Flower, say, for beastly female

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word sounding like it

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, i.e. a river, here the Tigris

explanation.surface: A bloom is offered as a name for a nasty woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword river: the Tigris of Iraq. Spoken, it matches the female big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A female of the striped big cat is a beast in the literal sense.

clue.text: Suits for naval officers?

parts.note: card suits are each one fourth of a pack, and the officers' part of a warship's upper level carries the same name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' suggests uniforms; it means the four suits of a pack of cards, each a quarter of the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear upper deck of a warship is reserved for officers, and a card suit is a quarter of a pack.

clue.text: Martial strife initially, could make one easily frightened

indicators.note: could make says the letters can be made into a new word by rearranging them
initially means the first letter of the word strife is taken

explanation.surface: Fighting talk might produce someone jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: MARTIAL plus S (the first letter of 'strife') is rearranged, signalled by 'could make'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises needless panic is quick to take fright themselves.

clue.text: Complete collection of books-in the country

indicators.note: in places the books inside the name of the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of biblical books

explanation.surface: A full set of books is to be found somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and whole are synonyms, both meaning with nothing missing.

clue.text: Foreigner's wife and daughter kept out of crime

indicators.note: kept out of means the letter is removed from the word for the crime

parts.note: fraud is a crime of deception

explanation.surface: An overseas woman and her daughter were not involved in the offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Frau is German for wife or Mrs, so it is a foreign wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for a married woman, used in English for a German wife.

clue.text: Revives debauchees at university

parts.note: rakes are dissolute, debauched men
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Libertines at college get a new lease of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revives' here means brings back old matters, as in raking up the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge up an old grievance is to bring it back into discussion, reviving it.

clue.text: Part of Oxford with impertinence for top people

parts.note: an Oxford is a laced shoe, and the upper is the part above the sole
crust is old slang for cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: A cheeky part of the university town produces the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the city; it is a type of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The aristocracy is the social elite, likened to the top crust of a loaf.

clue.text: MCC XI needing another four to time this historic declaration

definitions.text: MCC XI needing another four to time this historic declaration

parts.words: MCC XI needing another four to time this historic declaration
parts.note: MCCXI is Roman 1211; four more gives MCCXV, 1215, the year the barons' charter was sealed

explanation.walkthrough: MCC XI looks like a cricket team (the Marylebone Cricket Club eleven) and four like a boundary, but it is Roman numerals for a date.
explanation.definitionFit: The charter King John sealed at Runnymede in 1215 is a celebrated historic declaration of rights.

clue.text: Omit captain

definitions.meaning: to leave out or pass over
the leader of a team, especially in curling or bowls

explanation.definitionFit: To pass over something is to leave it out, and a team leader in bowls is the same word.

clue.text: Some job at hand? We'll soon see

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone with a task to do promises results before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like the verb; it is a bishop's diocese, here the Somerset diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and this one is the Church of England's diocese in Somerset.

clue.text: Passion required for section of contest

definitions.meaning: strong feeling, as in the warmth of the moment
a preliminary race or round in a competition

explanation.definitionFit: Intense emotion is warmth of feeling, and a qualifying round of a race shares the word.

clue.text: Mars green, going mad for a birdie

indicators.note: going mad means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A golfer goes wild on a putting surface to score one under par.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birdie' suggests golf; it simply means a small bird, a diving duck.
explanation.definitionFit: This saw-billed diving duck is a bird, 'birdie' being a playful word for one.

clue.text: Dubious confession of child's supporter left inside

indicators.note: inside means the letter goes within the phrase

parts.note: a supporter of a baby might confess: I'm pro babe

explanation.surface: Someone backing a youngster makes a doubtful admission.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase I'M PRO BABE is what a backer of a child would say; L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlikely to be true is doubtful, hard to believe.

clue.text: Teacher giving mark I dwell on

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the German mark currency
to stress a point is to dwell on it

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher grades a pupil and lingers over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman schoolteacher was traditionally addressed by this title in British schools.

clue.text: It can form a new phrase

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Something is able to coin an expression never heard before.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that forms or moulds something gives it its shape.

clue.text: Get king to sign as our representative

parts.note: John was king of England from 1199 to 1216
the bull, Taurus, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A monarch is persuaded to put his signature to a deal on behalf of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: JOHN BULL is the cartoon figure who personifies England or Britain, hence 'our' in a British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The stout farmer figure is the traditional personification of the English nation.

clue.text: Buffer in games

definitions.meaning: a set of games in bridge or whist, often best of three

explanation.definitionFit: A polisher rubs, and a match of three bridge games carries the same name.

clue.text: This sort of pupil may be repelled by crew

definitions.meaning: a pupil who lives in at school during term
someone climbing onto a ship uninvited, whom sailors fight off

explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' suggests school; the second half reads only as someone climbing aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil living at school during term shares the name for someone who forces a way onto a vessel.

clue.text: Times associated with firm in producing inventions

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
ages are long periods of time

explanation.surface: A newspaper teams up with a business to create something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly invented words or phrases are coined, so a coined term is a fresh creation.

clue.text: Lass one spies in part of Spain

parts.note: gal is a casual word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A young woman spots secret agents in a Spanish region.
explanation.definitionFit: This region in the north-west corner is an autonomous community of the Spanish state.

clue.text: Hermitage, say? There's benefit in silent surroundings

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the other
surroundings says the word for silent encloses the word for benefit

parts.note: mum means saying nothing
use means benefit, as in of some use

explanation.surface: A recluse's retreat gains from a quiet setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hermitage' suggests a hermit's cell; it is the great St Petersburg gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hermitage in St Petersburg is a famous example of an art gallery and collection.

clue.text: Jet-stream north of Manchester

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
burn is a Scottish and northern word for a stream

explanation.surface: A high-altitude air current sits above a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet-stream' looks like the high wind; split, it gives two pieces. Blackburn is a Lancashire town a little north of Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancashire town lies some twenty miles north-west of the city of Manchester.

clue.text: Uncultivated area of variable value

definitions.meaning: a card whose value the holder may choose, as in a joker

explanation.definitionFit: Untamed land is wilderness, and a card in poker that can stand for any rank shares the word.

clue.text: Joint pronunciation of Eliza and the dean

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle, the Cockney flower girl of Pygmalion, drops her aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: a hinge is a joint on which a door swings

explanation.surface: Eliza and a clergyman share a way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: W. R. Inge was the noted 'Gloomy Dean' of St Paul's Cathedral in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer William Ralph Inge was Dean of St Paul's, famous as the Gloomy Dean.

clue.text: Ordered to take notes

parts.note: B, A, D and E are all notes of the musical scale, each giving one letter
B, A, D and E are all notes of the musical scale, each giving one letter
B, A, D and E are all notes of the musical scale, each giving one letter
B, A, D and E are all notes of the musical scale, each giving one letter

explanation.surface: Someone was told to jot things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take notes' suggests writing; the word is built from musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is the past tense of bid, meaning commanded.

clue.text: Party man about to meet local organizer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a local is a pub, and the person who runs it is its landlord

explanation.surface: A political activist goes to see a community organiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Grand Old Party is a party man in American politics.

clue.text: Make gross

definitions.meaning: to make money, as in make a living
to gross is to take in as total income

explanation.definitionFit: To make or gross a sum is to take it in as pay or income.

clue.text: Limited in scope — for those with scruples?

definitions.meaning: a scruple is a tiny apothecaries' weight, so weighing them needs a little balance

explanation.definitionFit: Modest in extent describes a minor project, and tiny weights need a little balance.
